title: SharePoint: agent access heatmap for SharePoint and OneDrive sites
summary: The heatmap's paths, licence requirement and reporting limits are documented, and the roadmap facts match. The page overstates that data collection always requires new administrator action and omits the Copilot licensing prerequisite for restricted content discovery.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans an agent activity heatmap for SharePoint and OneDrive to detect patterns, hotspots and unusual access behaviour.
claims.quote: SharePoint: Agent Access Insights heatmap for SharePoint and OneDrive sites; Provides a visual heatmap of agent activity to help admins quickly detect patterns, hotspots, and unusual access behavior.

claims.quote: In the SharePoint admin center, expand Agent governance, select Agent access heatmap, and turn on data collection if it isn't already on.
claims.fix: In the summary replace 'An admin has to turn on data collection and generate a report' with 'An admin generates a report and turns on data collection if it is not already on'. Replace 'If nobody acts, nothing is collected' with 'An admin must generate insights; data collection may already be on'. Do not equate manual report generation with a universally off collection default. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/agent-access-heatmap-overview.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The page presents restricted content discovery as an available site action without qualifying its entitlement beyond the heatmap's Agent 365 or E7 prerequisite.
